docs.title: Parental leave policy
docs.body: At Tidewater Analytics, we recognize the importance of family and support our employees during significant life events such as the birth or adoption of a child. Our parental leave policy is designed to provide a comprehensive framework that balances the needs of employees with those of the company. Effective January 1, 2024, all eligible employees will be entitled to parental leave in accordance with this policy. Employees who have been with Tidewater Analytics for at least 12 months and have worked a minimum of 1,250 hours in the preceding year are eligible for parental leave. This includes both full-time and part-time employees who meet these criteria. The standard duration of paid parental leave will be 12 weeks for primary caregivers and 6 weeks for secondary caregivers. Primary caregivers are defined as the employee who takes on the majority of childcare responsibilities during the first year following the birth or adoption of a child. Secondary caregivers are typically partners or spouses who share in caregiving responsibilities but do not take on the primary role. In cases where both parents work at Tidewater Analytics, they may choose to split their leave, allowing them to take a combined total of up to 18 weeks. To ensure that all employees are informed about their options, we encourage employees to formally request parental leave at least 30 days prior to the expected date of leave whenever possible. Requests can be submitted through our internal HR tool, Employee Central, which allows for easy tracking and management of leave requests. Employees should provide documentation regarding their expected dates and any necessary supporting information. In cases of emergency or unforeseen circumstances, we will make every effort to accommodate requests made with less notice. During parental leave, employees will continue to receive their regular salary and benefits. This includes health insurance coverage at the same level as when they were actively working. Employees will not lose any accrued vacation time or sick days while on parental leave, ensuring that they can return to work without any financial detriment or loss of benefits. As part of our commitment to supporting our employees’ family needs, Tidewater Analytics also offers flexible work arrangements upon return from leave. Employees returning from parental leave will have the right to resume their previous positions or an equivalent position with similar pay and benefits. We understand that transitioning back into work after a significant life change can be challenging; therefore, we encourage open communication with managers and HR representatives during this transition period. Additionally, we offer a phased return-to-work program that allows new parents to gradually increase their hours over a four-week period if needed. In order to promote inclusivity and support diverse family structures, our parental leave policy extends beyond traditional maternity and paternity scenarios. We recognize that numerous family dynamics exist today, including same-sex couples and single parents, all of whom will be treated equitably under this policy. Furthermore, Tidewater Analytics is committed to maintaining an inclusive environment; hence any employee experiencing difficulties accessing their entitled leave should reach out directly to HR for assistance. If you have questions regarding your eligibility or need further clarification about our parental leave policy, please do not hesitate to contact your direct supervisor or HR representative. We are committed to providing resources and support during this important time in your life.

docs.title: Vendor security review process
docs.body: At Tidewater Analytics, ensuring the security of our vendor relationships is critical to our operational integrity and customer trust. As of January 2024, we have implemented a robust Vendor Security Review Process that is designed to assess and mitigate risks associated with third-party vendors. This process encompasses several phases, including initial screening, in-depth assessment, remediation, and continuous monitoring. Each vendor engagement will trigger the security review process, requiring completion within 30 days from the date of contract negotiation initiation. The Vendor Security Review Process is overseen by the Security Compliance Team, led by Sarah Thompson, our Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). The team comprises five dedicated security analysts who specialize in third-party risk assessments and cyber risk management. To facilitate this process, we utilize a proprietary tool called VetSecure Pro, which automates the assessment workflow and provides real-time analytics on vendor compliance status. During the initial screening phase, vendors must complete a comprehensive questionnaire that covers key areas such as data handling practices, security certifications (such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2), and incident response protocols. This initial questionnaire must be submitted within 10 days of the initial request; failure to do so could result in immediate disqualification from the review process. After receiving the questionnaire, our analysts will score vendors based on a predefined risk matrix ranging from low to high risk. Vendors categorized as high risk will be subject to an in-depth assessment that includes a review of their cybersecurity policies and procedures. The in-depth assessment phase typically lasts up to 15 days. During this phase, our analysts may request documentation such as penetration test results from the past year and evidence of employee training programs focused on data protection. We expect vendors to demonstrate adherence to industry best practices; for instance, they must have conducted at least one internal security audit within the last 12 months. Furthermore, all assessed vendors will be required to maintain liability insurance coverage of no less than $1 million per occurrence. Once all necessary information has been gathered and evaluated, any identified vulnerabilities or compliance gaps will be documented in a remediation plan drafted by our analysts. This plan will outline specific actions required from the vendor within a stipulated timeframe — typically no longer than 30 days — to address any issues before final approval can be granted. Continuous monitoring is an integral part of our Vendor Security Review Process. Once a vendor is engaged and approved, they will be subject to quarterly reviews through VetSecure Pro’s monitoring capabilities. This includes automated alerts for any changes in their compliance status or reported incidents that could impact their security posture. Additionally, we will conduct annual reassessments for all approved vendors to ensure ongoing compliance with Tidewater Analytics' standards. To ensure transparency throughout this process, all findings and assessments will be documented in our centralized compliance management system by Jane Doe, our Compliance Manager. She is responsible for maintaining records of all vendor assessments for a minimum period of five years. Any significant findings or breaches must be reported directly to senior management within one business day to facilitate prompt decision-making. In summary, the Vendor Security Review Process at Tidewater Analytics is designed to safeguard against potential threats posed by third-party vendors while maintaining operational efficiency. By adhering to rigorous assessment protocols and leveraging advanced tools like VetSecure Pro, we ensure that our partnerships are secure and compliant with industry regulations.

docs.title: Kafka migration plan
docs.body: Tidewater Analytics has initiated a comprehensive migration plan to transition from our existing messaging system to Apache Kafka, aiming to enhance our data processing capabilities and scalability. The project is scheduled to begin on January 15, 2024, and is expected to be completed by March 30, 2024. The migration effort will be led by Sarah Thompson, the Senior Data Engineer, with support from the IT operations team and the software development team. Our current system, based on ActiveMQ, has been experiencing latency issues, particularly with peak loads exceeding 10,000 messages per second. This migration addresses these challenges by leveraging Kafka’s distributed architecture, which can handle up to 1 million messages per second under optimal conditions. To ensure a smooth transition, we have developed a phased approach consisting of three distinct stages: Assessment, Migration, and Validation. During the Assessment phase, which will last from January 15 to February 1, 2024, we will conduct a thorough analysis of our existing message flows and data structures. This phase will involve collaboration with various department heads to identify critical workloads that must be prioritized during the migration. Following the assessment period, the Migration phase will commence on February 2 and continue until March 15, 2024. This stage includes setting up the Kafka cluster on our cloud infrastructure using AWS MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka), configuring topics based on our data model, and implementing producers and consumers in parallel with existing systems. We anticipate that this phase will require approximately six weeks of intense development work from both the engineering and QA teams. During the Migration phase, we will also implement necessary changes in our applications to accommodate Kafka’s architecture. The team will utilize Confluent’s Schema Registry to manage data schemas effectively and ensure compatibility across services. Additionally, we plan to set a message retention policy of seven days for most topics while allowing for longer retention periods for critical data streams that require historical analysis. The final stage of our plan is Validation, scheduled for March 16-30, 2024. In this phase, we will conduct rigorous testing of the new Kafka setup before full-scale production deployment. This includes load testing where we intend to simulate peak loads of at least 20% above our normal operational capacity as recorded in previous months' metrics. We expect this validation period to reveal any potential bottlenecks or issues that need addressing before we switch over completely. To facilitate communication during this project, we have established a dedicated Slack channel titled #kafka-migration where team members can post updates and questions. Regular check-ins are planned every Wednesday at 10 AM starting January 17 through March 27 to track progress against our timeline and resolve any arising issues promptly. In terms of training requirements post-migration, all relevant personnel must complete a two-hour workshop on Kafka operations by April 5, led by John Lee from Confluent. This training aims to ensure that all team members are proficient in managing our new messaging system effectively. The budget allocated for this migration project is $150,000 which covers infrastructure costs associated with AWS MSK services as well as training expenses for staff. We believe this investment is crucial for positioning Tidewater Analytics at the forefront of data processing technology within our industry.

docs.title: Design doc: feature flag service
docs.body: Tidewater Analytics is embarking on the development of a new feature flag service, aimed at enhancing our product development workflows and facilitating more agile release management. The purpose of this service is to allow the engineering teams to toggle features on and off in production environments without the need for redeploying code, thus enabling more controlled experiments and faster iterations on user feedback. The initiative is spearheaded by Jessica Chang, the Director of Software Engineering, who has set a target launch date of March 1, 2024. The feature flag service will be built using a microservices architecture, leveraging our existing cloud infrastructure based on AWS and Kubernetes, which has proven effective for our other applications. The decision to use this architecture was influenced by the need for scalability and ease of integration with our current tech stack, which includes tools like Docker for containerization and Terraform for infrastructure management. In terms of functionality, the feature flag service will include several core capabilities: the ability to create, update, and delete flags through a user-friendly dashboard; real-time updates to flags without downtime; and robust logging features for auditing purposes. We expect that over 50% of our product teams will adopt this service within six months of launch, based on initial surveys conducted among the engineering staff. To ensure that we meet this adoption goal, we are investing in comprehensive training sessions scheduled for late February 2024. The estimated budget for the development of this feature flag service is $150,000, which includes costs for development resources, infrastructure provisions, and training materials. According to our financial projections, we anticipate a return on investment within one year post-launch as teams realize efficiency gains in their release cycles. Specifically, we expect that deployment times will improve by approximately 30%, reducing from an average of four hours to around two hours per deployment. To keep stakeholders informed throughout the development process, bi-weekly sprint reviews will be held every other Wednesday starting January 10, 2024. These reviews will provide visibility into progress and allow for any necessary adjustments to timelines or resource allocations. In addition to sprint reviews, a dedicated Slack channel will be created for ongoing discussions and updates related to the feature flag service. This channel will help foster collaboration among team members across different departments. The feature flag service will also require stringent security measures to protect sensitive data and ensure compliance with industry standards such as GDPR and CCPA. We plan to implement role-based access control (RBAC) that restricts feature management capabilities based on user roles within the organization. Additionally, all data transactions related to flag changes will be encrypted both in transit and at rest using AES-256 encryption standards. To validate that we are meeting performance benchmarks post-launch, key performance indicators (KPIs) have been established: successful toggling of features must occur with less than ten seconds latency; at least 99.9% uptime must be maintained; and user satisfaction ratings should exceed 85% within three months following deployment. Regular monitoring against these KPIs will be carried out using our existing monitoring tools such as New Relic and Grafana. In conclusion, the design and implementation of Tidewater Analytics’ new feature flag service represent a significant strategic initiative intended to streamline our software delivery processes. By enabling features to be toggled dynamically in production environments without impacting system stability or downtime, we believe this service will enhance our ability to innovate rapidly while maintaining high-quality standards in our products.

docs.title: Expense reimbursement policy
docs.body: At Tidewater Analytics, we strive to maintain a transparent and efficient expense reimbursement process for all employees. This policy outlines the procedures and guidelines that employees must follow when submitting expenses related to business activities. All employees are encouraged to familiarize themselves with this policy to ensure compliance and timely reimbursement. The company will reimburse reasonable and necessary expenses incurred during the performance of job duties, provided they are pre-approved by the employee's direct supervisor. Employees must submit their expense reports within 30 days following the completion of the business activity. Any expenses submitted beyond this timeframe may be denied reimbursement unless prior exceptions have been explicitly granted by department heads. To facilitate the expense submission process, Tidewater Analytics utilizes an internal tool called ExpenseTrack, which allows employees to upload receipts, categorize expenses, and track the status of their reimbursements. Employees should ensure all receipts are legible and clearly indicate the date, amount, vendor, and purpose of the expense. For travel-related expenses, such as airfare or lodging, prior approval is required from the employee's direct supervisor at least two weeks before the trip is scheduled. Travel bookings should be made through our designated travel agency, TravelWise, to secure corporate rates and ensure compliance with our travel policies. The following are eligible for reimbursement: transportation costs (including mileage at $0.58 per mile for personal vehicle use), lodging (up to $150 per night), meals (up to $50 per day), and necessary materials or supplies purchased for work purposes. Meals must include a valid receipt showing the date and total amount spent; alcoholic beverages will not be reimbursed under any circumstances. Employees are responsible for ensuring that their submitted expenses comply with these guidelines. All requests will be reviewed by finance personnel within 10 business days of submission. If any discrepancies or issues arise during this review period, employees will be notified via email and given an opportunity to rectify any problems before final approval is granted. In cases where an employee feels that an expense denial is unjustified, they may appeal the decision in writing to their department head within 5 business days of receiving a denial notice. The department head will review the appeal and make a final determination within 7 business days thereafter. Employees should also keep in mind that any fraudulent submissions may result in disciplinary action up to termination of employment. Tidewater Analytics takes compliance seriously and expects all employees to act with integrity when submitting expense reports. This policy will be reviewed annually by the Finance Department to ensure it meets current operational needs and remains compliant with applicable regulations. Any changes or updates to this policy will be communicated to all employees via email no later than January 15 each year. docs.title: Design doc: tide forecasting model v4
docs.body: This document outlines the design and implementation plan for Tidewater Analytics' tide forecasting model version 4 (TFM v4), due to be completed by March 15, 2024. The primary goal of TFM v4 is to improve the accuracy of our tide predictions by at least 15% compared to the previous version, TFM v3, which had an accuracy rate of 82%. The project owner, Dr. Emily Carter, has assembled a cross-functional team consisting of data scientists, marine biologists, and software engineers to ensure that we leverage diverse expertise throughout the development process. This team will utilize Python as the primary programming language, along with TensorFlow for machine learning capabilities and PostgreSQL for data management. The data inputs for TFM v4 will include historical tide data from NOAA dating back to 1990, as well as real-time meteorological data such as wind speed and atmospheric pressure. We aim to incorporate at least 100,000 unique tide observation records into our model training dataset by December 1, 2023. docs.title: Sales commission plan
docs.body: At Tidewater Analytics, we are committed to recognizing and rewarding the hard work of our sales team through a structured and transparent sales commission plan. This plan aims to incentivize our sales representatives for their performance while aligning their efforts with the overall goals of the company. The commission structure is designed to motivate individual contributions towards achieving quarterly sales targets and fostering long-term client relationships. Effective from January 1, 2024, the commission plan will be in place for a full calendar year, with annual reviews scheduled to ensure competitiveness and alignment with market standards. All eligible employees must be in a sales role for at least three months before they can participate in the commission program. The sales team includes Account Executives, Sales Managers, and Business Development Representatives who work collaboratively to drive revenue growth. The commission structure is primarily tiered based on monthly sales performance. For every dollar generated in gross revenue up to $50,000, representatives will earn a base commission of 5%. Once sales exceed $50,000 within a month, the commission rate increases to 7% for any revenue generated from $50,001 to $100,000. Beyond $100,000 in monthly sales, representatives will earn an impressive 10% commission on all additional revenue generated within that month. For example, if an Account Executive generates $120,000 in a month, they would earn $2,500 from the first $50,000 (5%), $3,500 from the next $50,000 (7%), and $2,000 from the final $20,000 (10%), totaling a commission of $8,000 for that month. In addition to monthly commissions based on individual performance, there are also quarterly bonuses for teams that achieve or exceed their targets. If a team reaches 125% of their quarterly goal set at $300,000 by the end of March 2024, each member will receive a bonus of $2,500. This bonus structure encourages teamwork and collective responsibility towards shared goals. The sales team will use Salesforce CRM as their primary tool for tracking leads and managing client relationships. All sales figures must be entered into Salesforce by the end of each month for commissions to be calculated accurately. In order to streamline this process and ensure clarity in reporting, all representatives are required to submit their final figures by the last working day of each month. Tidewater Analytics also recognizes exceptional performance through an annual Sales Excellence Award. The recipient of this award will receive a cash prize of $10,000 along with an all-expenses-paid trip to the annual industry conference held in Las Vegas every October. The winner is selected based on highest total commissions earned over the fiscal year along with qualitative factors such as client feedback and teamwork. To foster ongoing development and success within our team members, there are mandatory training sessions scheduled bi-annually. These sessions focus on best practices in sales techniques and product knowledge enhancement. The next training session is set for May 15-16, 2024; attendance is crucial as it directly correlates with performance metrics evaluated during quarterly reviews. It’s important to note that any discrepancies or disputes regarding commissions must be reported within seven days following each month's close. A dedicated team led by Sales Operations Manager Emily Rodriguez will handle such inquiries promptly to ensure transparency and trust within our sales operations. We believe that this comprehensive plan not only provides competitive compensation but also fosters an environment where our teams can thrive together while achieving exceptional results for Tidewater Analytics.

docs.title: Postmortem: Harborview dashboard outage
docs.body: On October 12, 2023, Tidewater Analytics experienced a significant outage of its Harborview dashboard, which is a crucial tool for monitoring client data analytics. The incident began at approximately 9:30 AM EST and lasted until 2:15 PM EST, resulting in a total downtime of four hours and forty-five minutes. During this period, approximately 120 clients were unable to access their real-time analytics data, impacting their decision-making processes significantly. The outage was traced back to a failure in the backend database management system (DBMS), specifically within the Oracle Database version 19c that we utilize for data storage and retrieval. The initial alert indicating a potential issue came through our monitoring tool, Datadog, at 9:20 AM when CPU utilization for the DBMS exceeded 95% for over ten minutes. Our on-call engineer, Sarah Thompson, was notified immediately and began diagnostics but was unable to pinpoint the root cause within the first hour. By 10:30 AM, it became clear that the issue was not related to network connectivity or application-level errors based on logs from our error tracking tool, Sentry. As the situation unfolded, Sarah escalated the issue to the engineering team lead, Mark Johnson, at around 11:00 AM. The team quickly convened a war room session to address the critical downtime affecting multiple clients. By utilizing tools like Grafana for real-time monitoring and analysis of performance metrics, they discovered that a recent batch job scheduled to run at 9:00 AM had consumed an excessive amount of resources due to an unexpected increase in data volume. The batch job was designed to aggregate client data for reporting purposes but had not been optimized for the current influx of data from last quarter’s growth in user activity. It became apparent that we had not adjusted our thresholds or resource allocation settings in response to this surge. At around noon, after implementing an immediate rollback of the batch job and reallocating resources on our Oracle DBMS instance, system performance began to stabilize. By 1:45 PM, engineers confirmed that all services were back online and functioning normally. A thorough review of system logs indicated that all API calls had resumed successful execution by this time. However, post-incident analysis revealed that there was a significant delay in communication with affected clients during the outage; we sent an initial notification at 11:45 AM but did not provide follow-up updates until after service restoration at approximately 2:30 PM. In light of this incident, several corrective actions have been recommended to prevent similar occurrences in future operations. First and foremost is the need for enhanced monitoring thresholds that take into consideration historical data trends and expected spikes in usage. Additionally, it is crucial for us to implement more robust communication protocols during outages so that affected clients receive timely updates about service status. We will be conducting a follow-up meeting on October 19th with all stakeholders involved in dashboard operations to discuss these recommendations further and outline actionable steps moving forward. Furthermore, an internal training session will be scheduled before the end of October focusing on incident response strategies and effective communication with clients during outages.

docs.title: Partnership agreement summary with Meridian Ports
docs.body: This document summarizes the key points of the partnership agreement between Tidewater Analytics and Meridian Ports, finalized on February 15, 2023. This collaboration aims to enhance data analytics capabilities in port operations and logistics management. The agreement outlines the responsibilities of both parties, financial commitments, and the expected outcomes over a three-year period. Under this agreement, Tidewater Analytics will provide Meridian Ports with access to its proprietary analytics tool, PortInsight 2.0. This tool is designed to optimize cargo handling processes, improve turnaround times, and enhance overall operational efficiency. The deployment of PortInsight 2.0 is scheduled to begin on March 1, 2023, with full implementation expected by June 1, 2023. During this period, Tidewater will conduct training sessions for Meridian's staff to ensure they are proficient in utilizing the new system. Financially, the partnership involves an initial investment of $500,000 from Meridian Ports for the license of PortInsight 2.0 and associated services. Additionally, there is a revenue-sharing model established whereby Tidewater Analytics will receive 15% of any cost savings realized by Meridian Ports through improved operational efficiencies attributed to the use of PortInsight 2.0. This revenue-sharing agreement is set to last until March 1, 2026. To measure the effectiveness of this partnership, specific performance metrics have been established. These include a target reduction in cargo handling times by at least 20% within the first year of implementation and a decrease in operational costs by a minimum of $250,000 annually thereafter. Regular performance reviews will take place every six months to assess progress against these benchmarks. In addition to financial commitments and performance metrics, both parties have agreed on confidentiality terms regarding proprietary information shared during the course of this partnership. This confidentiality clause ensures that any sensitive data related to operational procedures or technological solutions remains protected from external disclosure. The agreement also stipulates that either party may terminate the contract with a written notice period of 90 days if performance expectations are not met or if there are significant changes in business conditions that affect either party's ability to fulfill their obligations. Should termination occur before the completion of the three-year term, any outstanding financial liabilities will need to be settled within 30 days. Tidewater Analytics is represented by its CEO, Sarah Thompson, who has been instrumental in forging this partnership due to her previous experience in logistics analytics. On Meridian Ports' side, John Mitchell serves as the Director of Operations and has expressed strong support for leveraging advanced analytics tools to drive efficiency in their operations. As part of future developments under this agreement, a joint innovation task force will be created that includes members from both companies. This task force will focus on exploring additional applications of data analytics within port operations beyond what is covered under the current scope with PortInsight 2.0.

docs.title: Design doc: sonar ingestion service
docs.body: The sonar ingestion service at Tidewater Analytics is designed to process and analyze sonar data collected from various marine environments, providing critical insights for our clients in the fisheries and oceanography sectors. The project, spearheaded by John Whitaker, is scheduled to initiate its development phase on March 15, 2024, with an expected completion date of September 30, 2024. The primary goal of this service is to handle and transform data from multiple sonar devices into a standardized format suitable for further analysis and reporting. Our current estimates suggest that the system will need to manage an influx of approximately 2 terabytes of raw sonar data weekly, originating from around 500 active sonar units deployed across different coastal regions. This ingestion service will utilize Apache Kafka as the backbone for streaming data processing due to its ability to handle high throughput with low latency, making it ideal for real-time analytics requirements. In terms of infrastructure, we plan to deploy the ingestion service on AWS using a microservices architecture. Each microservice will be responsible for specific functions such as data normalization, error handling, and storage management. The services will communicate through RESTful APIs and will ensure a modular approach that allows for easy updates and maintenance. We anticipate that each microservice will require approximately 2 weeks for development and testing before integration into the overall system. For data storage, we have decided to use Amazon S3 combined with Amazon Redshift for long-term analytics purposes. The decision was influenced by S3's durability and scalability, allowing us to retain historical data up to five years. This retention policy aligns with our clients’ needs for trend analysis and regulatory compliance in their operations. Additionally, we are implementing monitoring tools such as Prometheus and Grafana to track system performance metrics including ingestion speed, error rates, and downtime incidents. Security is another significant concern; therefore, all sensitive data will be encrypted both at rest and in transit using AES-256 encryption standards. Access control lists (ACLs) will be enforced to ensure that only authorized personnel can access sensitive information related to our clients’ datasets. Furthermore, we are implementing a logging mechanism using ELK (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) stack which will allow us to audit access and modifications made within the system. To ensure high availability and fault tolerance, we plan on deploying the service across multiple AWS regions with an active-active configuration that automatically handles failover scenarios. Our target uptime commitment is set at 99.9%, which requires rigorous testing during both development and pre-production phases. The testing phase will include load testing with simulated sonar data streams designed to mimic expected real-world usage patterns. The project team consists of eight members including frontend developers, backend developers, a database administrator, and a quality assurance engineer. Regular sprint reviews every two weeks will provide transparency into progress while allowing us to adapt quickly based on stakeholder feedback. As part of our agile methodology, we aim to incorporate client feedback throughout the development process through bi-weekly demos scheduled starting April 1st. In terms of budget allocation, we have earmarked $250,000 for this project which includes costs related to personnel salaries over the six-month development period as well as cloud infrastructure expenses estimated at around $50,000 during the implementation phase.

docs.title: Layoff communication plan (confidential)
docs.body: In light of recent market conditions and the need to streamline operations, Tidewater Analytics has developed a layoff communication plan to guide our management team through this difficult process. Effective immediately, we will begin the necessary steps to reduce our workforce by 15%, which equates to approximately 30 positions across various departments. This decision was not made lightly; it is driven by a significant decline in revenue projections for Q4 2023, which have fallen to 20% below our original estimates. The affected teams include Product Development, Marketing, and Customer Support, with the majority of reductions occurring in the Product Development department, where we anticipate cutting 12 positions. The timeline for this reduction will span from November 1 through November 30, allowing for adequate notice and support for impacted employees. The first step in our communication plan involves an all-staff meeting scheduled for October 30, where we will outline the rationale behind these layoffs and address employees' concerns. Following this meeting, department heads will conduct one-on-one sessions with their teams before any formal notifications are sent out. These sessions are designed to foster an open dialogue and provide employees with a platform to express their feelings and seek clarification on next steps. After the initial announcement on October 30, formal layoff notifications will be delivered by November 15. Employees selected for layoff will receive a severance package that includes two weeks’ pay for every year of service, capped at a maximum of six months’ pay. Additionally, we are committed to assisting affected employees in their transition by providing access to career counseling services through our partner firm, CareerPath Solutions. These services will be available until December 31, 2023. Employees who are laid off will also retain health benefits until the end of their severance period. Throughout this process, it is essential to maintain confidentiality and respect for those affected. We expect all employees to refrain from discussing specific details related to individual layoffs outside of official communications. Any breach of confidentiality may result in disciplinary action as per company policy. To facilitate communication during this challenging time, we have established a dedicated support channel via our internal tool, TideConnect. Employees can submit questions or concerns anonymously through this platform starting October 31. We aim to respond within one business day to ensure clarity and support throughout the transition period. In addition to addressing employee needs directly, we will also communicate externally regarding these changes. A press release is scheduled for November 16 that will address the restructuring while emphasizing our commitment to remaining a leader in analytics solutions despite current challenges. Our leadership team recognizes the emotional toll that layoffs can take on both those who are departing and those who remain with us. Therefore, we encourage everyone at Tidewater Analytics to utilize available resources such as Employee Assistance Programs (EAP) and mental health services during this time of uncertainty.
